rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan surah has five verses.
rows.anchor: سورة المسد مكية وآياتها خمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab was Muhammad’s uncle, ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; his bright face gave him the nickname Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: هو عم النبي [ ص ] وإنما سمي أبو لهب لإشراق وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm Jamil, Arwa daughter of Harb ibn Umayya and Abu Sufyan’s sister, supported her husband’s sustained campaign against Muhammad and the message.
rows.anchor: وكانت زوجته أم جميل في عونه في هذه الحملة الدائبة الظالمة .

rows.speaker: ربيعة بن عباد الديلي
rows.claim: Rabiʿa recalls accompanying his father as a youth, seeing Muhammad preach to tribes while Abu Lahab followed, warning them against abandoning al-Lat and al-ʿUzza for his alleged innovation.
rows.anchor: ربيعة بن عباد الديلي يقول :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports Muhammad warned Quraysh from al-Baṭḥāʾ; Abu Lahab retorted, “Was that why you gathered us?”, after which the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،  أن النبي [ ص ] خرج إلى البطحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant says Abu Lahab shook his hands and cursed Muhammad for the rest of the day, again prompting revelation of the surah.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية فقام ينفض يديه وهو يقول : تبا لك سائر اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Banu Hashim agreed under Abu Talib to protect Muhammad out of clan solidarity, Abu Lahab defected to Quraysh and joined their boycott document.
rows.anchor: ولما أجمع بنو هاشم بقيادة أبي طالب على حماية النبي [ ص ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab had betrothed his sons to Muhammad’s daughters before the mission, then ordered them to divorce the women to burden Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وكان قد خطب بنتي رسول الله [ ص ] رقية وأم كلثوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is reported that Umm Jamil carried thorns and put them in Muhammad’s path.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أن أم جميل كانت تحمل الشوك فتضعه في طريق النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes carrying firewood figuratively as her pursuit of harm, discord, and backbiting against the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن حمل الحطب كناية عن سعيها بالأذى والفتنة والوقيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah answers the public war Abu Lahab and his wife waged; God undertakes the battle on behalf of His Messenger.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه السورة ترد على هذه الحرب المعلنة من أبي لهب وامرأته .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabb means ruin, destruction, and severance; the first occurrence is a supplication, the second confirms that it has come to pass.
rows.anchor: والتباب الهلاك والبوار والقطع . ( وتبت )الأولى دعاء . ( وتب )الثانية تقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a single short opening verse the curse is issued and fulfilled, ending the conflict and drawing its curtain.
rows.anchor: ففي آية قصيرة واحدة في مطلع السورة تصدر الدعوة وتتحقق ،  وتنتهي المعركة ويسدل الستار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab’s wealth and earnings could not benefit him, fend off ruin, or prevent his destruction.
rows.anchor: فلم يغن عنه ماله وسعيه ولم يدفع عنه الهلاك والدمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After his worldly destruction Abu Lahab will burn in the afterlife; describing the fire as flaming makes its blazing vivid.
rows.anchor: ويذكر اللهب تصويرا وتشخيصا للنار وإيحاء بتوقدها وتلهبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab’s wife will burn alongside him in the condition of carrying firewood.
rows.anchor: وستصلاها معه امرأته حالة كونها حمالة للحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masad is palm fiber; she is bound with it in Hell, or it is the rope binding firewood, literally if thorns are meant and figuratively if firewood means evil.
rows.anchor: تشد هي به في النار .  أو هي الحبل الذي تشد به الحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The images correspond: Abu Lahab burns in flame while his wife brings fuel and binds it; her punishment uses the same wood-and-rope elements as her deed.
rows.anchor: والحطب مما يوقد به اللهب .  وهي تحزم الحطب بحبل .  فعذابها في النار ذات اللهب أن تغل بحبل من مسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound of “Tabbat yadā Abī Lahab wa-tabb” evokes the force of binding wood, tightening it, and pulling a rope at the neck, matching the surah’s angry threat.
rows.anchor: تجد فيها عنف الحزم والشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musical sound, the noise of work, coordinated images, verbal pairing, and the occasion of revelation combine in five brief clauses.
rows.anchor: وهكذا يلتقي تناسق الجرس الموسيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vivid, mocking image made a proud Umm Jamil think the Prophet had composed poetry to satirize her, especially through the wood-carrier and rope around her neck.
rows.anchor: هذا التناسق القوي في التعبير جعل أم جميل تحسب أن الرسول [ ص ] قد هجاها بشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reports that Umm Jamil came to the Kaaba mosque with a fist-sized stone, could see only Abu Bakr, and threatened the Prophet over supposed satire.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق : فذكر لي أن أم جميل حمالة الحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Abu Bakr asked whether she had seen him, Muhammad said God had taken her sight away from him until she left.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو بكر : يا رسول الله ،  أما تراها رأتك ? فقال : ما رأتني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar transmits Ibn ʿAbbas’s report: Abu Bakr feared Umm Jamil might harm Muhammad, but the Prophet said she would be screened from him; she accused his companion of satire.
rows.anchor: وروى الحافظ أبو بكر البزار - بإسناده - عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that report Abu Bakr denied Muhammad was a poet; after she left, the Prophet said an angel had screened him from her sight.
rows.anchor: ما زال ملك يسترني حتى ولت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm Jamil was enraged because she thought the proclamation was poetry, since satire was conventionally composed as verse; Abu Bakr’s denial was truthful.
rows.anchor: وكان الهجاء لا يكون إلا شعرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eternal scripture and the record of existence preserve her degrading caricature; schemers face worldly ruin and ridicule, afterlife fire, and humiliation symbolized by the rope in both worlds.
rows.anchor: والذل الذي يشير إليه الحبل في الدنيا والآخرة جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ is Meccan and has four verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الإخلاص مكية وآياتها أربع

rows.speaker: أبو سعد
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari reports from Abu Saʿd that a man told the Prophet about another man repeatedly reciting the surah; the Prophet swore it equals one third of the Quran.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه ،  عن أبي سعد ،  أن رجلا سمع رجلا يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb calls the report unsurprising because the surah’s oneness is a creed, an interpretation of existence, and a way of life, containing Islam’s principal outlines.
rows.anchor: هذه الأحدية عقيدة للضمير ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥad is more precise than wāḥid: it asserts that nothing else is with God and nothing resembles Him.
rows.anchor: أن لا شيء غيره معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is real being and reality; every other existent derives its being and truth from His self-subsisting reality.
rows.anchor: وكل موجود آخر فإنما يستمد وجوده من ذلك الوجود الحقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone acts in anything or acts upon anything in the universe; this oneness is both creed and an account of existence.
rows.anchor: في شيء ،  في هذا الوجود أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Settled recognition of God’s unique reality and agency frees the heart from attachments to everything else.
rows.anchor: خلص القلب من كل غاشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With no independent existence or agency besides God, desire and fear lose their hold: nothing is lost with God and no other force can be feared.
rows.anchor: وفيم يرغب وهو لا يفقد شيئا متى وجد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One spiritual degree sees God’s hand in everything; a further degree sees nothing in the cosmos except God, since only His reality is real.
rows.anchor: وهذه درجة يرى فيها القلب يد الله في كل شيء يراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawhid denies independent causal power, returning every event and movement to the first cause, God; the Quran repeatedly connects events directly to His will.
rows.anchor: ورد كل شيء وكل حدث وكل حركة إلى السبب الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By setting apparent causes aside and referring affairs to God’s will, the heart gains calm and knows where to seek what it wants and protection from what it fears.
rows.anchor: تنسكب في القلب الطمأنينة ،  ويعرف المتجه الوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sufis pursued these stations but were drawn too far; Islam requires pursuing the truth while engaging fully in real human life and earthly vicegerency.
rows.anchor: وهذه هي مدارج الطريق التي حاولها المتصوفة ،  فجذبتهم إلى بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawhid yields a life-method of worshipping God alone and turning to Him alone in desire and fear, prosperity and adversity.
rows.anchor: ومنهج للاتجاه إلى الله وحده في الرغبة والرهبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It requires receiving beliefs, values, laws, institutions, customs, and norms from God alone, the sole true reality in the world and conscience.
rows.anchor: ومنهج للتلقي عن الله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It requires working for God and seeking nearness to truth by overcoming inner and outer barriers, including the self and its desires and fears.
rows.anchor: ابتغاء القرب من الحقيقة ،  وتطلعا إلى الخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freedom from attachment does not mean hating or fleeing creatures: all come from God and draw existence from Him, so each is a gift from the Beloved.
rows.anchor: فكلها إذن حبيب ،  إذ كلها هدية من الحبيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic liberation is not withdrawal, neglect, hatred, or escape; it is sustained struggle to elevate all humanity and liberate human life while bearing leadership’s duties.
rows.anchor: والكفاح الدائم لترقية البشرية كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Monastic escape is easy but rejected: earthly leadership is a harder divine route to salvation that realizes human nature and the spirit’s victory in its assigned field.
rows.anchor: إن الخلاص عن طريق الصومعة سهل يسير .  ولكن الإسلام لا يريده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first call focused on establishing tawhid in hearts because it is the whole religion and a life-method; further details naturally grow from it.
rows.anchor: من أجل هذا كله كانت الدعوة الأولى قاصرة على تقرير حقيقة التوحيد بصورتها هذه في القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier distortions among the People of Scripture began when pure tawhid was obscured, followed by other deviations.
rows.anchor: نشأت أول ما نشأت عن انطماس صورة التوحيد الخالص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic tawhid must shape practical life and legislation; God’s law alone must govern, and without these effects tawhid is not truly established.
rows.anchor: وأول هذه الآثار أن تكون شريعة الله وحدها هي التي تحكم الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṣamad means the master to whom needs are directed and by whose permission affairs are decided; God alone is master, sought, responsive to need, and judge of every affair.
rows.anchor: السيد المقصود الذي لا يقضى أمر إلا بإذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attribute follows from God’s being uniquely one: none decides alongside Him, and He alone answers those who seek help.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي يقضي في كل أمر بإذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s reality is eternal, immutable, and absolutely perfect in every state; it undergoes no succession of conditions.
rows.anchor: لا تعتورها حال بعد حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birth entails extension and added existence after lack, plus a paired likeness; both are impossible for God, so oneness entails having neither parent nor child.
rows.anchor: ووجود زائد بعد نقص أو عدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No being equals God in reality, agency, or any intrinsic attribute; this is implied by oneness but stated for emphasis and detail.
rows.anchor: أي لم يوجد له مماثل أو مكافئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rejects dualism, which posits a good God and an opposing evil deity that reverses His good works and spreads corruption.
rows.anchor: وهو نفي للعقيدة الثنائية التي تزعم أن الله هو إله الخير وأن للشر إلها يعاكس الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best-known dualist creed was the Persian doctrine of a god of light and a god of darkness, familiar in southern Arabia under Persian power.
rows.anchor: وأشهر العقائد الثنائية كانت عقيدة الفرس في إله النور وإله الظلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ affirms Islamic tawhid, while al-Kāfirūn denies any overlap between tawhid and polytheism; the Prophet opened the dawn’s sunnah prayer with both.
rows.anchor: كما أن سورة  " الكافرون "  نفي لأي تشابه أو التقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Falaq is Meccan and has five verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الفلق مكية وآياتها خمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Falaq and al-Nās direct the Prophet first, then all believers, to seek God’s shelter from every feared thing, known or unknown, apparent or hidden.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة والتي بعدها توجيه من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb presents the refuge as a tender invitation from God: come to His protective shelter, where the weak can find safety, reassurance, and peace amid enemies and fears.
rows.anchor: في مودة وعطف : تعالوا إلى هنا

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir reports that the Prophet said no verses like al-Falaq and al-Nās had ever been revealed as those revealed that night.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة - ابن عامر - رضي الله عنه - أن رسول الله

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet instructed him to recite both refuge surahs and said he would read nothing comparable to them.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر - رضي الله عنه - قال : قال لي رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Qutb notes that Ibn Masʿūd initially did not include the two surahs in his codex, then returned to the community’s view and included them.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود لا يثبتهما في مصحفه ثم ثاب إلى رأي الجماعة وقد أثبتهما في المصحف

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Dharr ibn Ḥubaysh reports that Ubayy ibn Kaʿb asked the Prophet about the two surahs and heard that he had been told to recite them; Muslims follow that instruction.
rows.anchor: وعن ذر بن حبيش قال : سألت أبي بن كعب - رضي الله عنه - عن المعوذتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports all convey the affectionate, sheltering quality of the refuge that the Prophet experienced deeply and joyfully.
rows.anchor: وكل هذه الآثار تشي بتلك الظلال الحانية الحبيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falaq can mean dawn or all creation, encompassing what existence and life split forth from; Qutb links both senses to God’s signs in al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: ومن معانيه الخلق كله .  بالإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether dawn that dispels hidden darkness or the created world, seeking refuge with its Lord fits the request for protection from the evils that follow.
rows.anchor: وسواء كان هو الصبح فالاستعاذة برب الصبح الذي يؤمن بالنور من شر كل غامض مستور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request is general protection from evil among all creatures: they can harm one another, yet also bring good, which God can direct and manage so their good remains.
rows.anchor: والاستعاذة بالله هنا من شرها ليبقى خيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguistically, ghāsiq is flowing or pouring, and waqab is a hollow in a mountain from which water runs; the intended referent is probably night.
rows.anchor: والوقب النقرة في الجبل يسيل منها الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is frightening in itself and intensifies unseen dangers: predators, robbers, deceitful enemies, poisonous insects, worries, grief, devils aided by darkness, and desire in solitude.
rows.anchor: والليل حينئذ مخوف بذاته .  فضلا على ما يثيره من توقع للمجهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “blowers in knots” are sorceresses who seek harm by deceiving senses and nerves and suggesting effects to souls and feelings.
rows.anchor: السواحر الساعيات بالأذى عن طريق خداع الحواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tie knots in thread or cloth and blow into them as a customary practice of magic and suggestion.
rows.anchor: وهن يعقدن العقد في نحو خيط أو منديل وينفثن فيها كتقليد من تقاليد السحر والإيحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magic does not change things’ nature or create new reality; it only makes the senses and feelings imagine what the sorcerer intends.
rows.anchor: ولا ينشئ حقيقة جديدة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb uses Moses’s encounter in Ṭā Hā as the Quranic picture of magic: spectators imagined the ropes and staffs moving, but they had not actually become snakes.
rows.anchor: ولكن خيل إلى الناس - وموسى معهم - أنها تسعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses feared until reassured; the truth was exposed when his staff really became a serpent and swallowed the counterfeit ropes and staffs.
rows.anchor: ثم انكشفت الحقيقة حين انقلبت عصا موسى بالفعل حية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magic’s suggestion can frighten and hurt people and direct their feelings; Qutb says understanding its nature should stop at this point.
rows.anchor: مشاعر تخيفهم وتؤذيهم وتوجههم الوجهة التي يريدها الساحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports, described as sound but non-mutawātir, say the Jewish Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam bewitched the Prophet in Medina for days or months; versions differ about what he imagined doing.
rows.anchor: لبيد بن الأعصم اليهودي سحر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those reports say the two surahs were revealed as a healing recitation; after the targeted magic was found as in a vision and the surahs read, knots came undone and the harm passed.
rows.anchor: انحلت العقد ،  وذهب عنه السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb rejects these reports because they conflict with prophetic protection in action and transmission, and clash with Quranic rejection of the claim that the Prophet was bewitched.
rows.anchor: تخالف أصل العصمة النبوية في الفعل والتبليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says solitary reports cannot establish doctrine: the Quran is the reference and mutawātir transmission is required for foundational beliefs; these reports are not mutawātir.
rows.anchor: والتواتر شرط للأخذ بالأحاديث في أصول الاعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surahs’ likely Meccan origin further weakens the reports, which place the alleged magic in Medina.
rows.anchor: فضلا على أن نزول هاتين السورتين في مكة هو الراجح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Envy is a psychological response to God’s favor on another person, accompanied by wishing that the blessing disappear; harm can follow whether or not the envier acts on it.
rows.anchor: والحسد انفعال نفسي إزاء نعمة الله على بعض عباده مع تمني زوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should temper denial of mysteries of existence and the human psyche: telepathy has repeated reports and experiments but no known explanation, as does hypnosis.
rows.anchor: هنالك مثلا ذلك التخاطر على البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because knowledge and tools reveal little, one cannot rule out an envier’s directed psychological effect merely because its mechanism remains unexplained.
rows.anchor: فلا سبيل لنفي أثر هذا التوجيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Envy is therefore an evil from which people should seek God’s shelter.
rows.anchor: فهنا شر يستعاذ منه بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directs the Prophet and his community to seek refuge and certainly protects them from these evils when they do so, generally and specifically.
rows.anchor: والله برحمته وفضله هو الذي يوجه رسوله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari reports from ʿĀʾisha that each night the Prophet joined his palms, blew into them, recited al-Ikhlāṣ and both refuge surahs, then wiped his body from head and face down, repeating three times.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة - رضي الله عنها - أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان إذا آوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Nās is Meccan and has six verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الناس مكية وآياتها ست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refuge names God as Lord, King, and God of humanity; protection is sought from the hidden retreating whisperer, who whispers in people’s hearts, whether jinn or human.
rows.anchor: الاستعاذة في هذه السورة برب الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invoking these divine attributes calls to mind the powers that repel evil generally and the whisperer’s evil in particular; the Lord nurtures, directs, cares for, and protects.
rows.anchor: فالرب هو المربي والموجه والراعي والحامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The King is owner, ruler, and disposer; the God is exalted, possessing, and controlling. These attributes protect against evil that creeps unseen into hearts.
rows.anchor: والملك هو المالك الحاكم المتصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God is Lord, King, and God of all things, naming humanity specifically evokes closeness while seeking shelter.
rows.anchor: ولكن تخصيص ذكر الناس هنا يجعلهم يحسون بالقربى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In mercy God directs the Prophet and community to invoke Him against a hidden creeping evil they cannot repel without divine help, which approaches unexpectedly.
rows.anchor: لا قبل لهم بدفعه إلا بعون من الرب الملك الإله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasa is a faint, hidden sound; khunūs means hiding or retreating, and khannās describes one who habitually withdraws.
rows.anchor: والوسوسة : الصوت الخفي . والخنوس : الاختباء والرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage first names the whisperer by a general trait, then defines its action and finally its kinds; this sequence awakens vigilance to recognize its nature and method and prepare to watch or resist it.
rows.anchor: وهذا الترتيب يثير في الحس اليقظة والتلفت والانتباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the suspense, people learn that the whisperer secretly enters hearts; both hidden jinn and human agents creep in and whisper like devils, enabling the soul to prepare defense at the entry point.
rows.anchor: يوسوس في صدور الناس خفية وسرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: How jinn whisper is unknown, but its effects appear in souls and life; the struggle between Adam and Iblis is ancient, driven by the devil’s evil nature, pride, envy, and rancor toward humanity.
rows.anchor: ووسوسة الجنة نحن لا ندري كيف تتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis obtained God’s permission to wage this war, granted for divine wisdom; God equipped people with faith as armor, remembrance as provision, and seeking refuge as a weapon.
rows.anchor: فقد جعل له من الإيمان جنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who neglects this armor, provision, and weapon is responsible for standing alone against whispering.
rows.anchor: فإذا أغفل الإنسان جنته وعدته وسلاحه فهو إذن وحده الملوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet’s saying that Satan crouches on a person’s heart: remembrance makes him withdraw, while heedlessness lets him whisper.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - قال : قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human whispering is familiar and can be worse than satanic whispering: a trusted bad companion stealthily plants harm in a friend’s heart and mind.
rows.anchor: وأما الناس فنحن نعرف عن وسوستهم الشيء الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evil courtiers whisper to rulers until they become tyrants who corrupt the land and destroy crops and people.
rows.anchor: وحاشية الشر التي توسوس لكل ذي سلطان حتى تتركه طاغية جبارا مفسدا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A talebearer prettifies and slides words until they seem like undeniable truth; a seller of lusts exploits instinct unless the heart stays alert and seeks God’s help.
rows.anchor: والنمام الواشي الذي يزين الكلام ويزحلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Countless crafty human whisperers hide traps and exploit hidden entrances to hearts, moving more subtly than jinn; people cannot repel such hidden whispers unaided.
rows.anchor: وعشرات من الموسوسين الخناسين الذين ينصبون الأحابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the whisperer khannās portrays both stealth while it waits and weakness when a vigilant person protects the heart: confronted, it retreats and hides again.
rows.anchor: فهو - سواء كان من الجنة أم كان من الناس - إذا ووجه خنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This image strengthens believers against whispering, but the battle never ends: the whisperer waits for lapses, and vigilance must recur until the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: فهو خناس .  ضعيف أمام عدة المؤمن في المعركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb links the ongoing conflict to the Quran’s account of Iblis’s rebellion, his request to mislead Adam’s descendants, and God’s permission and warning in al-Isrāʾ.
rows.anchor: وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God controls all creation and holds Iblis in check, humans are not helpless: satanic influence has no power over those who remember God, while good relies on the only true power.
rows.anchor: فإن ربه وملكه وإلهه مسيطر على الخلق كله وإذا كان قد أذن لإبليس بالحرب فهو آخذ بناصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between powerful good and a weak whisperer who retreats before refuge in God is the fullest account of good and evil and the best protection against despair.
rows.anchor: والشر يستند إلى وسواس خناس يضعف عن المواجهة
